section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Distinctive Appearance Investment Scale (Tiggemann & Golder, 2006), a 6-item measure using a 5-point Likert scale with items averaged to form a total score; higher scores indicate greater desire for a unique appearance. Internal consistency in the current study is reported (women α = .76, men α = .82). The section does not provide sample size, demographics, country, BMI information, body appreciation measures, or study numbering.
section_summary.evidence_source: Full section text: "The Distinctive Appearance Investment Scale (Tiggemann & Golder, 2006) was used to measure desire for uniqueness in the appearance domain (sample items: \"I use my physical appearance to express who I am,\" \"When it comes to appearance, I am somewhat of a non-conformist.\"). It has 6 items to which participants respond on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = Strongly disagree to 5 = Strongly agree). Items were averaged to create a total score, with higher scores indicating stronger desire for a unique appearance. Previous research demonstrates the validity and reliability of scores on this measure in men and women (Swami, 2011; Tiggemann & Golder, 2006; Tiggemann & Hopkins, 2011). Internal consistency reliability scores in the current study were adequate (women ˛= .76, men ˛= .82)."
